# Drive kernel-ready@1

Generated by `maestro flow driver-skill` from the compiled IR of kernel-ready@1 (`sha256:f422375564f441f5ecd448f6304aff502f8bdf38e02f605bbfb431eeb76f2bc3`). Do not edit it: change the definition and generate it again. It says only in what order to drive the flow. The kernel decides what may run, and each node's own skill says how to do it well.

Every verb is a `maestro flow` subcommand with `--json`, and the MCP tool `maestro_flow_<verb>` takes the same arguments as JSON. A write acts for your verified session. In a T3 thread it needs no session and no credential: Maestro attributes it to the thread your process's own thread variable names (`T3CODE_THREAD_ID`, or `CODEX_THREAD_ID` in a Codex shell), and refuses it if that thread is not the one you name. Claude writes over MCP or the CLI. Codex writes through the CLI, from its shell: its MCP server carries no thread variable, so an unsigned Codex write over MCP is refused (`attribution_missing`), as is every unsigned Gemini write, until BRO-3848. Elsewhere, name your session with `--session` (or `MAESTRO_SESSION`) on the CLI and `session` over MCP. The CLI reads your claim from the environment: a Direct launch token (`MAESTRO_DIRECT_TOKEN` with `MAESTRO_CALLER_CWD`) or a bridge credential (`MAESTRO_BRIDGE_CREDENTIAL`). Over MCP, pass it in each write's arguments: `cwd` and `token` for a Direct session, `credential` for a T3 or Paseo session, and `node` for the tailnet node your session runs on.

## Start or resume

- Params: `consumer`, `head`, `repo`, `suite`, `surface`, `writer_provider` (required).
- Start on the CLI: `maestro flow start --definition <path to the kernel-ready@1 definition file> --params '<json>'`. `--definition` is a file path (`-` reads the YAML from stdin).
- Start over MCP: `maestro_flow_start` with `definition` holding the definition's YAML text itself, never a path, and `params` as a JSON object. When the definition declares `agents:`, also pass its absolute file path as `definition_path`.
- Either way, the `ir_hash` it returns must be `sha256:f422375564f441f5ecd448f6304aff502f8bdf38e02f605bbfb431eeb76f2bc3`; another hash is another definition, which this skill does not drive.
- Resume: keep the instance id `flow start` returned; every verb below takes it.

## The loop

Whether to stop is decided by the kernel (`terminal`, in step 1 and step 4), never by reading node states yourself.

1. Run `maestro flow status --instance <I> --json` (`maestro_flow_status`). First, `status.ir_hash` must be `sha256:f422375564f441f5ecd448f6304aff502f8bdf38e02f605bbfb431eeb76f2bc3`: an instance whose hash is another runs another definition, so stop and report it, and apply none of this skill's nodes to it. Then, if `status.terminal` is `true`, stop: report each node's state and the accepting spine, `flow spine --instance <I>` (`maestro_flow_spine`). The flow is done; a node blocked by a branch not taken never runs, and that is not a failure.
2. Run `maestro flow next --instance <I> --json` (`maestro_flow_next`). Do each node in `next.enabled` as The nodes below says, in any order: `flow claim --instance <I> --node-id <N>` (`maestro_flow_claim`) gives a `claim_token`; finish with `flow complete --claim-token <T>` (`maestro_flow_complete`, `--outputs '<json>'` for a performer's work) or, for a choice, `flow choose --claim-token <T> --edge <E>` (`maestro_flow_choose`). Heartbeat a long claim with `flow heartbeat --claim-token <T>` (`maestro_flow_heartbeat`). An enabled node's `launch_spec` of `kind: agent` says how your harness launches its agent; one of `kind: unknown_agent` cannot be launched, so stop and report it.
3. For each `relay` entry `flow next` returned, run `flow ask --instance <I> --node-id <N>` (`maestro_flow_ask`). An `unfiled` entry needs `--ledger` and `--ask` the first time, to file its ask. An `owner` or `answer_waiting_to_land` entry needs nothing more: only `flow ask` reads main, so it is what takes an answer that has landed there. `state: answered` means the node is done; `state: waiting` means the owner has not answered on main yet.
4. Then, in this order:
   - If `next.terminal` is `true`, the flow is done: stop and report, as step 1 says.
   - If a repeat in `status.repeats` has `awaiting_verdict: true`, its `until` could not be judged when its body settled (an error or a timeout). Retry it with `flow claim --instance <I> --node-id <the first node of its body, as Repeats lists it>`: a claim judges every pending verdict before anything else. A `claim_token` means the verdict moved the repeat on: do that node as step 2 says, then go back to 1. A refusal: go back to 1. After 3 such claims with the repeat still awaiting its verdict at the same iteration, stop and report: its `until` fails over that input every time. (3 is this skill's bound, `maestro_flow::driver::VERDICT_RETRIES`: an `until` is jq over the same input each time, so an error repeats, and only a timeout under load, at the kernel's 1 s guard timeout, can pass on a later try.)
   - If `work` (beside `next` in step 2's result) was empty and step 3 filed no ask and took no answer, nothing is yours to do now: the instance waits on someone else, as `waiting` names (the owner's answer to a filed ask, or a former owner's claim until its lease ends). Stop and report what `waiting` and `relay` name; the instance stays open. `work` is the kernel's judgment of what you can do now, the same one Maestro's Stop-hook gate reads (`maestro_flow::kernel::stop`): while it is not empty, the gate refuses your final message.
   - Otherwise, go back to 1.

A refusal is a result, not an error: read its `code`. After `lease_expired` or `cancelled`, claim the node again; after `not_enabled`, go back to 1. A pure node's `verify_failed` means its command failed, and a pure command fails the same way again: stop and report it, never retry it. A human node's answer comes from the owner through the asks ledger, never from you.

## The nodes

In the order the flow enables them. A node comes after everything it waits on; the nodes of one step do not wait on each other.

### Step 1: `pin`

#### `pin` (observe)

- Waits on: nothing.
- Do: claim it, then complete it with no outputs. The kernel runs its command and records its value: exit 0 is `pass`; any other exit fails it. It is fresh for 7200 s; once stale, `flow next` enables it again, and everything after it waits for the new value.

### Step 2: `suite`

#### `suite` (pure)

- Waits on: `pin`.
- Do: claim it, then complete it with no outputs. The kernel runs its command in a snapshot of the commit `{{params.head}}` names, never in the working tree. A refusal `verify_failed` means the command failed, and a pure command fails the same way again: stop and report it.

### Step 3: `installed`

#### `installed` (observe)

- Waits on: `suite`.
- Do: claim it, then complete it with no outputs. The kernel runs its command and records its value: exit 0 is `pass`; any other exit fails it.

### Step 4: `mcp_tools`

#### `mcp_tools` (observe)

- Waits on: `installed`.
- Do: claim it, then complete it with no outputs. The kernel runs its command and records its value: exit 0 is `pass`; any other exit fails it.

### Step 5: `stop_gate`

#### `stop_gate` (observe)

- Waits on: `mcp_tools`.
- Do: claim it, then complete it with no outputs. The kernel runs its command and records its value: exit 0 is `pass`; any other exit fails it.

### Step 6: `consumers`

#### `consumers` (observe)

- Waits on: `stop_gate`.
- Do: claim it, then complete it with no outputs. The kernel runs its command and records its value: exit 0 is `pass`; any other exit fails it.

### Step 7: `exercise`

#### `exercise` (work)

- Waits on: `consumers`.
- Performer: `agent:verifier`, with the skill `dogfood`.
- Routed (BRO-3828): its performer's provider must differ from `params.writer_provider`. Delegate the work to a child session of yours (a T3 thread you delegate to, or a direct session you launch) on another provider, and name it on `flow complete` with `--performer-session <its session>` (`performer_session`); naming it on `flow claim` too only checks it early. Completed without one, the performer is you, and the kernel refuses `routing_violated` when your provider is excluded; `performer_unverified` means the session is not your child on this host, or ran more than one provider.
- Do: claim it; launch the `verifier` agent (see Agents) with the node's task; then complete it with what that returns as its outputs. The kernel runs the node's verify on them. A refused completion keeps the claim while its lease holds: repair from the refusal's reason and stderr, and complete again with the same claim token.

### Step 8: `ready`

#### `ready` (human)

- Waits on: `exercise`.
- Do: nothing to claim. File its ask with `flow ask` (the first call takes `--ledger` and `--ask`), then call `flow ask` again until it says answered. The owner answers `Is the Maestro flow kernel at {{params.head}} ready? Every check of kernel-ready@1 passed for this head: its suite, the installed binary, the MCP tools, the Stop gate for Claude Code and Codex, the consumers, and an exercise by a provider other than the writer's.`; never answer it yourself.

## Agents

Give the agent the node's task: the flow (kernel-ready@1), the instance, the node and the instance's params (`consumer`, `head`, `repo`, `suite`, `surface`, `writer_provider`). It returns the node's outputs; you claim and complete the node, never the agent.

### `verifier`

Exercises a declared surface of a repository at a pinned commit the way a user would, and writes a dogfood-receipt@1 with its evidence. Use it for a Maestro flow's exercise node (verify@1).

Its source is `agents/verifier.agent.yaml`. Launch it through your harness:

- Claude Code: the `Agent` tool with `subagent_type: "verifier"` (`.claude/agents/verifier.md`).
- Gemini CLI: the `invoke_agent` tool with `agent_name: "verifier"` and the node's task as `prompt` (`.gemini/agents/verifier.md`).
- Grok: the `spawn_subagent` tool with `subagent_type: "verifier"` (`.grok/agents/verifier.md`).
- Codex: the `spawn_agent` tool with these arguments, the node's task appended to `message` (`task_name` only where your `spawn_agent` takes one):

```json
{
  "message": "You are the verifier. A Maestro flow driver launched you for one node: exercise the surface it\nnames, at the commit it names, the way a user would, and leave a receipt the kernel can check.\n\nThe task you are given names the repository, the head (a full commit id) and the surface. If\nthe repository's HEAD (`git -C <repo> rev-parse HEAD`) is not the head, say so and stop.\n\nExercise the head's content only, never the repository's working tree, which can hold changes\nno commit has. Make an isolated checkout of the head in a new temporary folder:\n`git clone --quiet --shared --no-checkout <repo> <tmp>`, then\n`git -C <tmp> checkout --quiet --detach <head>`. Never use `git worktree add`, which writes into\nthe repository. Check that `git -C <tmp> rev-parse HEAD` is the head and that\n`git -C <tmp> status --porcelain` prints nothing; if either fails, write a receipt whose result\nis \"fail\" and stop. Build and run the surface from that folder alone, and remove it when you are\ndone.\n\nUse the dogfood skill: reach the surface through its real entry (a URL, a command, a window),\ndrive it with a real driver (curl, a browser driver, a shell), and keep what shows the result\n(a log, a screenshot, a response body) as one evidence file.\n\nThen write the receipt, one JSON object with exactly these fields:\n\n- `schema`: \"dogfood-receipt@1\"\n- `head`: the head you were given, as given\n- `surface`: the surface you were given, as given\n- `entry`: what a user touches first\n- `driver`: what drove it\n- `evidence`: {\"path\": the evidence file, absolute or relative to the receipt's folder, \"sha256\": \"sha256:\" and its 64 hex digest}\n- `result`: \"pass\" only when the surface did what a user needs; otherwise \"fail\"\n- `at`: when you drove it, an RFC 3339 timestamp\n\nWrite the receipt and the evidence as regular files, never symbolic links, outside the\nrepository (a temporary folder will do), and change nothing in the repository. The kernel\nchecks the receipt with `maestro dogfood verify-receipt`; it refuses one that names another\nhead or surface, says fail, or whose evidence no longer hashes to its digest. Do not call any\nmaestro_flow tool yourself: the driver claims and completes the node with what you return.\n\n## Skills\n\nUse these skills: `dogfood`.\n\n## Tools\n\nRead and search files, and run shell commands. Use no edit tool: write a file only from the shell, and only where your role says.\n\n## What you return\n\nReturn exactly one JSON object that matches this JSON Schema, and nothing else. The driver completes the flow node with it.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"properties\": {\n    \"receipt\": {\n      \"description\": \"The receipt's path, absolute or relative to the repository.\",\n      \"type\": \"string\"\n    },\n    \"receipt_sha256\": {\n      \"description\": \"The receipt file's digest.\",\n      \"pattern\": \"^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$\",\n      \"type\": \"string\"\n    }\n  },\n  \"required\": [\n    \"receipt\",\n    \"receipt_sha256\"\n  ],\n  \"type\": \"object\"\n}\n```\n",
  "model": "gpt-6.1-terra",
  "task_name": "verifier"
}
```
